oneliner.t: Yup'ik Democrat and former U.S. representative (Sept 2022–Jan 2025), the first Alaska Native in Congress, who lost the House seat to Nick Begich in 2024 and led the Aug. 18, 2026 Senate primary with 49.5%.

born.note: Date from Wikipedia; Anchorage birthplace also in her Alaska Beacon questionnaire. Her election pamphlet says only 'Alaska'.

hometown.t: Bethel, Alaska (raised along the Kuskokwim River)

upbringing.t: Daughter of Ward Sattler, a Nebraska-born pilot and teacher, and Elizabeth 'LizAnn' Williams, a Yup'ik woman from Kwethluk. She grew up in Kwethluk, Tuntutuliak, Platinum and Bethel, began fishing with her father at six and registered as a fishing captain at 14. She studied elementary education at the University of Northern Colorado (1991–93) and took courses at three University of Alaska campuses (1994–98) without a degree listed. Her husband Eugene 'Buzzy' Peltola Jr. died in a September 2023 plane crash; she has four children and three stepchildren.

profile.office_years_note: Alaska House 1999–2009 (10) + Bethel City Council 2011–2013 (2) + U.S. House Sep 2022–Jan 2025 (~2.3). Tribal court judge 2020–21 not counted.

education.deg: Coursework in elementary education, no degree listed
education.school: University of Northern Colorado; UAF, UAS, UAA

platform.t: Running on lowering gas, grocery, health care, housing and childcare costs; says she would cut taxes and raise wages.

Proposes 12-year congressional term limits, a ban on members and immediate families owning or trading individual stocks, the DISCLOSE Act ($10,000 disclosure threshold), and a constitutional amendment overturning Citizens United.
Would ban factory trawling, keep mid-water trawlers off the sea floor, seek fishery-disaster money and add Tribal seats to the North Pacific Fishery Management Council.
Says she supports oil and gas development; her September 2026 energy plan backs Alaska LNG and more in-state refining.
Opposes Medicaid cuts; would restore Medicaid money and reinstate ACA premium tax credits.
Says abortion decisions belong to a woman and her doctor; backs gun rights (NRA member per her pamphlet; NRA endorsed her in 2024).
Opposes the war with Iran and says she would have backed war-powers measures to halt it.

promises.t: Push 12-year congressional term limits and a congressional stock-ownership ban.
Ban factory trawling and reduce bycatch to restore salmon runs.
Reverse health-care cuts and fund the Alaska Marine Highway, the Railbelt grid, public radio and education.

claims.claim: Served in the Alaska House 1999–2009, on the Bethel City Council 2011–2013 and in the U.S. House 2022–2025.

said.where: 2026 election pamphlet bio (substitute — campaign 'My Story' page unreachable)

record.t: Same dates in Wikipedia and Ballotpedia (U.S. House Sept 13, 2022–Jan 3, 2025).

claims.claim: Lived in Bethel, Kwethluk, Tuntutuliak and Platinum before moving to Anchorage in 2025.

record.t: Wikipedia lists the same four Kuskokwim communities.

claims.claim: Attended the University of Northern Colorado, UAF, UAS and UAA.

record.t: UNC 1991–93 and University of Alaska campuses 1994–98; no degree listed (she does not claim one).

claims.claim: Executive Director, Kuskokwim River Inter-Tribal Fish Commission.

record.t: Wikipedia lists her as executive director after 2016; Ballotpedia says interim executive director. Whether she holds the job now was not confirmed.

claims.claim: Two of her sons have served in the U.S. Coast Guard.

record.t: Membership is not independently documented; the NRA did endorse her in 2024.

claims.claim: 'Pushed through the largest pay increase for our soldiers in decades.'

said.where: Peltola TV ad (most-covered ad #1, per FactCheck.org)

record.t: The 5.2% raise in the FY2024 NDAA was the largest in more than 20 years and she voted for the final bill, but the raise followed the statutory Employment Cost Index formula; FactCheck.org calls 'pushed through' subjective. Her one enacted NDAA amendment was unrelated to pay.

claims.claim: Introduced legislation to open ANWR and NPR-A to oil development.

said.where: campaign energy rollout (Sept 2026), as reported by Fox News (most-covered #2)

record.t: She co-led Alaska's Right to Produce Act with Rep. Pete Stauber in 2023, then urged Democrats to vote against the floor version over a provision nullifying the Northern Bering Sea Climate Resilience Area, and later filed a version without it.

claims.claim: She secured the reversal that let ConocoPhillips' Willow project move forward.

said.where: campaign energy rollout, per Fox News

record.t: She publicly backed Willow with both Alaska senators; sources reviewed do not show her role as decisive.

claims.claim: Sullivan remains the 'top recipient' of Big Trawl campaign cash.

record.t: The post relies on an opinion column and op-ed that give no figures; OpenSecrets industry data could not be reached.

claims.claim: Sullivan 'tripled his wealth in office' and made up to $2 million as a stock trader.

record.t: An Alaska Current review of disclosures says his trades roughly tripled his wealth, but its $2 million figure describes estimated trade volume, not profit. Disclosure ranges make exact gains unknowable.

Her 2025 House disclosure, as summarized by Newsweek, lists retirement and 529 accounts and 'some investments' but no itemized holdings were reviewed; the Alaska Current says she reported no trades in office.

said.t: 'I support oil and gas development'; touts bills to open ANWR and NPR-A.

did.t: Co-led Alaska's Right to Produce Act and voted for it in committee, then urged House Democrats to oppose the floor version over a Bering Sea provision; she later introduced a version without it.

said.t: House record broke with most Democrats in support of Israel.

did.t: Voted for the February 2024 stand-alone Israel aid bill (one of 46 Democrats) and in May 2024 for the bill to stop the administration from withholding arms to Israel (one of 16 Democrats). In 2026 her campaign would not say whether her views have changed.

said.t: Ad says she pushed through the largest troop raise in decades.

did.t: Voted for the final FY2024 NDAA containing the 5.2% raise (after voting against the House version in July 2023).

saydo.note: Same vote as the pay-raise claim in the claims check; scored once there.

promises_prev.promise: Restore salmon runs by curbing trawl bycatch (2022–24 House campaigns).

evidence.t: Introduced the Bottom Trawl Clarity Act and Bycatch Reduction and Mitigation Act in May 2024; neither became law before she left office.

complicating.t: 53 trawl interests and fishery stakeholders urged her to withdraw the bills, calling them unworkable. House Republicans controlled the floor in 2023–24.

entries.t: Co-chaired the Blue Dog Coalition (May 2023–Jan 2025) and voted with Republicans on several immigration-enforcement bills.
Called guns part of Alaska's culture and a core subsistence tool; NRA endorsed her in 2024.

aipac_endorse.t: Not checked on AIPAC's site. Track AIPAC lists no entry for her (as of 2026-10-08).

aipac_pac.note: 2024 cycle: 10 entries totaling $13,253 from the AIPAC PAC committee (C00797670) to Mary Peltola For Alaska, including a $5,000 contribution on Oct 25, 2024; the small entries are likely earmark pass-throughs (not confirmed). No AIPAC money to her 2026 Senate committee was found in the sources reached.

udp.note: No United Democracy Project spending for or against her was found; not confirmed absent.

israel.votes_note: Roll-call votes are handled by the key-vote pass (ak-votes.json). Descriptive record from news: voted for the Feb 2024 stand-alone Israel aid bill; voted for the May 2024 bill blocking the administration from withholding arms to Israel; backed ICC sanctions and several antisemitism resolutions; opposed censuring Rep. Tlaib.

statements.t: Her Senate campaign did not answer repeated questions about whether she still stands by her House Israel record.

fec.src_note: Jan 1–Jul 29, 2026. pac_all = FEC 'other committee contributions' (combined; split not available). In Q1 2026 PACs gave about $450,000 (~6%), mostly Democratic leadership PACs (Alaska Public Media). 'other' = $1,648,275.45 transfers from authorized/joint-fundraising committees + $35,457.43 residual (offsets/other receipts). Candidate self-funding not shown on the page. EMILY's List passed about $44,000 in earmarked gifts in Q1 2026 (inside itemized individual money).
fec.quarters_note: Q1 2026 per Wikipedia's FEC table (raised through Mar 31, 2026). Peltola spent about $1.4M on digital fundraising in Q1 (Alaska Public Media).

support: Democratic-aligned super PACs (unnamed in report) — more than $3M in Alaska ad buys by April 2026
oppose: Fair Deal Alaska — ~$152,000 opposing her (through Aug 8, 2026) out of more than $768,000 total, while boosting Green Richard Grayson and Democrat Carol ‘Kitty’ Hafner in the Senate primary; donors undisclosed until after the election
Last Frontier PAC (pro-Sullivan) — ads on the Sept 2026 NYT staff-treatment report and on troop pay; amount not found

fec.outside_note: FEC independent-expenditure tables did not load. Amounts are news-reported at the dates shown. Across the whole race, Alaska Public Media (Oct. 2, 2026) reports independent groups have spent more than $31 million since the Aug. 18 primary, about 70% on opposition; groups backing Sullivan have outspent groups backing Peltola by nearly $7 million.

U.S. House statement of candidacy filed Nov 8, 2024

corp.t: Corporate and trade PACs gave to her 2024 House campaign, including Exxon Mobil PAC, PricewaterhouseCoopers PAC, National Association of Realtors PAC, National Business Aviation Association PAC and National Marine Manufacturers Association PAC ($5,000 each), Halliburton PAC ($2,500) and Apache Corp. PAC ($2,000), per ProPublica's partial listing. Her 2026 Senate PAC money ($602,146 through Jul 29) is described as mostly Democratic leadership PACs in Q1.

lobby.t: Pro-Israel PAC money in 2024: $13,253 from the AIPAC PAC committee to her House campaign (including $5,000 on Oct 25, 2024) and $4,000 from DMFI PAC. None found for 2026.

money2.note: Donors to the Democratic-aligned super PACs backing her were not identified. Fair Deal Alaska (opposing her) has not disclosed donors.

networth.note: Campaign says $62,006–$230,000 (not from a reviewed disclosure). Her 2025 House filing (per Newsweek) lists retirement and 529 accounts of $15,000–$50,000 each, a $250,000–$500,000 mortgage and $10,000–$15,000 in credit-card debt.

trades.note: The Alaska Current says she reported no trades while in office.

note.t: House disclosures not read directly (search form not automatable). In 2025 she sued the company that owned the aircraft in her husband's fatal crash (she is plaintiff; no further detail).

committees: Education and the Workforce (Education and Labor)
effectiveness.note: 118th-Congress committee list on Ballotpedia was blank; Wikipedia lists 117th assignments. Sponsored/enacted counts not retrieved; congress.gov not reached.

revolving.t: Registered Alaska lobbyist between her state House service and her congressional run; clients not reviewed.

democracy_note: Not in Congress for the Jan 2017 or Jan 2021 counts and left office Jan 3, 2025, before the Jan 6, 2025 count. No search was run for her public statements on the 2020 or 2024 presidential results. She supports ranked-choice voting and the open primary.

access.note: Took part in a Kodiak fisheries debate with Sullivan and held town halls/meet-and-greets around the state (campaign posts); totals not compiled.

note.t: Lifelong Alaskan; lived in Bethel most of her life (1973–79, 1988–2025) and moved to Anchorage in 2025.

checks.legal: No CourtListener/Justia searches were run. House Ethics/OCE not searched. News reviewed shows no charges or lawsuits against her. The Sept 23, 2026 NYT report (via Newsweek) of former aides alleging she used slurs and once shoved a staffer is an unadjudicated allegation she denies; it is not a legal matter and is not entered under legal. Her 2023 office had the second-highest staff turnover in the House (Wikipedia).
checks.foreign: FARA not searched; House disclosures not read directly. No foreign ties surfaced in news reviewed.

research_notes: RACE: led the certified Aug 18 primary 49.5% (unofficial Aug 25 printout: 48.22%, 70,816 votes). NYT/Siena (Sept 24–Oct 1) had her +7; other September polls ranged from Sullivan +2 to Peltola +5. FEC: Senate committee C00933978 and all three House cycles read directly. She filed a House statement of candidacy on Nov 8, 2024 that stayed active into 2025 (the House committee raised $152K through Feb 13, 2026). The AIPAC total is from ProPublica's Itemizer rows for C00797670 → C00812388; whether the $1–$1,000 rows are earmarks was not confirmed. DAN J. SULLIVAN: Sullivan's campaign and the NRSC accuse her of recruiting the Petersburg Dan J. Sullivan. The only documented links are his consultant Amber Lee (who has worked for Democrats and publicly backed Peltola) and small 2022/2024 ActBlue gifts to her campaigns from 'a Dan Sullivan from Petersburg'. Her campaign denies any role, and the elections director cited no coordination evidence. These are claims about other people; nothing ties her campaign to the filing. NYT STAFF REPORT (Sept 23, 2026): former aides alleged slurs and one shove; the campaign denies them and cited grief over her husband's and mother's 2023 deaths. Reported here only as an allegation.
